_about: The architecture graph for implementation (roadmap Epic H): a derived copy of the architecture that agents query before they edit. Aligned with the architecture framework the model is written in (CALM through the calm pack's adapter; C4 when one exists) 1.0, the FINOS Common Architecture Language Model (https://calm.finos.org/release/1.0/meta/core.json): a CALM node is an estate node (System, Component, DataStore, Environment, Role) carrying its external_id and external_type; a CALM relationship is a Relationship node with its two ends, its kind and its protocol; controls (what they safeguard) and flows are nodes; and the implementation trace runs from a requirement with a budget, through the evidence that measured it, to the code modules and commits that implement a component, with change proposals raised by evidence and settled by decisions; a Contract is a version of an interface, frozen by a named person so consumer and provider build in parallel against it. On software-architecture, so the estate's questions keep answering. A relation is {domain, range, inverse, definition}. Use A|B for a union.
_summary: The architecture as agents consult it before they change code: CALM nodes, relationships, controls and flows as facts on the estate, requirements with budgets and the evidence that measured them, the code modules and commits that implement each component, and the change proposals evidence raised.
name: Architecture

Relationship.definition: A CALM relationship as a node of its own: what interacts with, connects to, is deployed in or composed of what, over which protocol, or the options a decision chooses between. A node because a flow walks it in order and a control governs it, which an edge could carry neither of.

Control.definition: A control the architecture declares, keyed by its CALM id: what it governs (a node, a connection, a flow) and the requirement schema it cites, with its configuration inline or by URL.

Flow.definition: A business or technical flow through the architecture: an ordered walk over relationships, named, described, and traceable to the requirement it serves.

FlowStep.definition: One step of a flow: its sequence number, the relationship it walks and the direction it walks it in.

NFR.definition: A non-functional requirement with a metric and a budget: the number a node must stay within (p95 latency, availability, cost), which measured evidence is checked against.

Evidence.definition: Something observed about the architecture at a date: a measurement, a test result, a review, a gate's verdict, a log. What a budget is checked against and what raises a change proposal.

CodeModule.definition: A unit of code that implements a component: a package, a directory, a module, at a path in a repository.

Commit.definition: A recorded change to code: the commit that changed a module, with its sha, date, author and message.

ChangeProposal.definition: A proposed change to the architecture, raised by evidence (a gate that failed, a measurement over budget), about the nodes, relationships or controls it would change, settled by a decision and implemented in a commit.

Contract.definition: A version of an interface the estate declares: an event schema, an API, a file layout, with a status that is a decision. A draft until a named person freezes it; frozen means nobody changes it without a new version that supersedes it, so a consumer and its provider build in parallel against it; retired once superseded.

connects_from.definition: The relationship's source end: the actor that interacts, the node a connection comes from, the container a deployment or a composition names.

connects_to.definition: The relationship's destination end: the nodes an actor interacts with, the node a connection goes to, the nodes deployed in or composing the container. One edge per node.

via.definition: The interface a connection goes through, at either end, when the model names one.

offers_option.definition: The decisions an options relationship chooses between, each a Decision until one is accepted.

contract_of.definition: The one interface this contract is a version of.

supersedes.definition: This replaced that. Use with the temporal fields, never by overwriting. Widened to the contract: a new version supersedes the old, which is retired.

safeguards.definition: What the control applies to: a node, a connection or a flow. Its own relation, apart from a decision's `governs`, so that what no control safeguards can be asked.

step_of.definition: The one flow a step belongs to.

over.definition: The one relationship a step walks.

measurement_of.definition: The requirement a measurement is checked against: the value against the budget.

evidence_of.definition: What the evidence is about: the node a gate judged, the connection a test exercised, the proposal a review supports.

implemented_by.definition: Where the component's code lives: the repository, and the modules inside it. Widened to the module, so a path answers.

located_in.definition: The repository a module's path is in.

prompted_by.definition: The evidence that raised the proposal: the gate that failed, the measurement over budget, the review that asked.

proposes_change_to.definition: What the proposal would change, so the siblings it affects are one walk away.

decided_in.definition: The decision that accepted or rejected the proposal.

implemented_in.definition: The commit that carried the accepted change into the code.

external_id.definition: The node's id in the framework its model was written in (CALM's unique-id, C4's identifier), so the node round-trips to that framework unchanged. A node authored in the graph may carry one too: the export writes it under that id.

external_type.definition: The node's type as the framework names it, kept as given, so the export writes it back unchanged; the class it maps to is the adapter's call (a database or a data asset is a DataStore, a network an Environment, an actor a Role, any other type a Component). Absent, the export uses the class's default.

external_payload.definition: What the framework carries about the node that no question asks for (metadata, details), kept as the JSON it gave and never read by the engine; the adapter writes it back as given.

external_id.definition: The interface's id in the framework (CALM's unique-id).

definition_url.definition: The URI of the schema the interface configuration conforms to (CALM interface-definition).

config.definition: The interface configuration as the model gave it, JSON, conforming to definition_url; or the typed interface's own fields.

external_id.definition: The relationship's id in the framework (CALM's unique-id).

kind.definition: Which of CALM's five relationship shapes this is.

protocol.definition: The protocol a connection speaks, from CALM's list.

external_payload.definition: What the framework carries about the relationship beyond its ends, kind and protocol (metadata), kept as the JSON it gave.

external_id.definition: The control's id, the key the framework files it under (letters, digits, hyphens).

requirement_url.definition: The requirement schema that specifies how the control is defined.

config_url.definition: Where the configuration meeting the requirement lives, when it is not inline.

config.definition: The inline configuration meeting the requirement, as the JSON the model gave.

external_id.definition: The flow's id in the framework (CALM's unique-id).

requirement_url.definition: The requirement the flow serves, by URL.

external_payload.definition: What the framework carries about the flow beyond its steps (metadata), kept as the JSON it gave.

sequence.definition: The step's place in the flow, from 1.

direction.definition: Which way the step walks the relationship.

metric.definition: What is measured: p95 latency of the journey, monthly availability, cost per request.

budget.definition: The number to stay within, with its unit: 900 ms, 99.9 %, 0.002 USD.

kind.definition: What sort of observation it is.

value.definition: What was observed, with its unit where it has one.

source_url.definition: Where the observation can be seen: the run, the report, the log.

path.definition: The module's path within its repository.

language.definition: The language it is written in.

author.definition: Who committed it, as git records it.

message.definition: The first line of the commit message.

status.definition: Where the proposal stands. Proposed when unsaid.

external_payload.definition: The option as the framework gave it (a CALM options relationship's decision), kept as JSON so the export writes it back unchanged.

framework.definition: The architecture framework the model was read with (calm), the name of the adapter that reads and writes it; `oto arch export --framework` finds the model by it.

external_payload.definition: The model's own header as the framework gave it (its schema, id, name, metadata, decision records), kept as JSON; the export starts from it.

version.definition: The contract's version, as its schema names it: 1, 2.1, 2026-10.

status.definition: Where the contract stands. A draft when unsaid; frozen by a named person (`oto decide`), the factory's freeze; retired when a new version supersedes it.

kind.definition: What sort of contract: an event's schema, an API, a data schema, a file layout.

schema_url.definition: Where the contract's schema is read: the file in the repository, or a URL.
